title: Commissioners' Meeting 04/28/25
tldr: With Commissioner McKelvey absent, the Board chose courthouse Option 2B: a 45,000 sq. ft. two-story courthouse estimated at $38.2 million, designed for a future 45,000 sq. ft. addition. It approved a performance-based incentive grant and a supporting resolution for Project Mound, a trail design and construction firm. The consent agenda included a $2,815,160 architect contract with LS3P for the school bond renovation projects, and the Board approved the third-quarter financial report and budget amendments. The Board also heard the Sheriff's semi-annual report, the school system's FY 2026 budget request (including two teacher supplement options), a capital projects update, a water and sewer planning briefing, and a Hurricane Helene recovery update.

keyVotes.description: Approved the meeting agenda as presented
Approved consent agenda, including a $2,815,160 LS3P architect contract for school bond renovation projects
keyVotes.background: The consent agenda included: minutes of the March 24 and April 14, 2025 meetings; the March 2025 tax discovery, release and settlement report (releases of $1,094.57 and refunds of $911.14); grant-funded out-of-state travel for the Public Health Region 1 Workforce Development Director; and proclamations for Older Americans Month, Historic Preservation Month, Foster Care Awareness Month and Clerks to the Boards of County Commissioners Week. It also included a $2,815,160 contract with LS3P for architectural services on all three scopes of the school bond renovation projects; the firm was selected by the Joint School Bond Project Committee through an RFQ process.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioner Chapman asked that the Clerks Week proclamation be read aloud and recognized Clerk to the Board Trisha Hogan for serving as President of the NC Association of County Clerks. Chairman Chappell thanked her for 18 years of service.

keyVotes.description: Reappointed Dwight Parker and Harold Paxton to the Agricultural Advisory Board
keyVotes.background: Both members' terms expired at the end of April, and both were eligible and willing to serve again. Cooperative Extension staff recommended their reappointment.

keyVotes.description: Approved performance-based incentive grant and Building Reuse grant resolution for Project Mound (28 jobs, $1.49 million investment)
keyVotes.background: Project Mound is a trail design and construction firm considering an existing building in the county for its headquarters and manufacturing hub. It plans 28 new jobs by 2029 with an average salary above $49,286, plus $1.49 million in investment. The project scored 75 on the County scorecard, qualifying it for a grant of 75% of ad valorem property taxes rebated annually for five years, contingent on meeting targets. Resolution #15-2025 supports the company's NC Building Reuse Program application, which requires a 5% County match. Transylvania Economic Alliance Executive Director Burton Hodges presented, and a public hearing earlier in the meeting drew no comments.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioners expressed support for the project and thanked Mr. Hodges for his economic development work.

keyVotes.description: Selected courthouse Option 2B: 45,000 sq. ft. two-story courthouse with a future 45,000 sq. ft. addition (estimated $38.2 million)
keyVotes.background: Sizemore Architects presented four programming options ranging from $38.2 million to $61.1 million. Option 2B is a 45,000 sq. ft. fully upfitted courthouse with two stories and a partial basement, designed for a future 45,000 sq. ft. two-story addition, with phased parking. Staff recommended limited obligation or general obligation bonds rather than USDA loans; $3.6 million in fund balance contributions is committed to the architectural contract. Design is expected to take about one year and construction about 18 months.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioner McCall asked about the design timeline and whether 3D renderings would be provided. Commissioner Chapman raised concern about upfitting shell space while court is in session. Commissioner McCall replied that phased construction is common, that 45,000 sq. ft. more than doubles current usable space, and that constituents had questioned the cost. Chairman Chappell said he had changed his earlier support for third-floor shell space based on fiscal considerations and architect input. Commissioner Chapman encouraged early visual materials for the public, and Commissioner McCall said the Board must plan for the future use of the existing courthouse.

keyVotes.description: Received the FY 2025 third-quarter financial summary
keyVotes.background: Finance Director Meagan O'Neal presented unaudited results through March 30, 2025. General Fund revenues were $62,975,652, including property tax at 97.7% of budget, and expenditures were $50,985,808. The Solid Waste enterprise fund showed net income of $267,360.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioner Chapman asked how long the County had banked with First Citizens and whether better rates had been explored. Ms. O'Neal said staff regularly review and negotiate services, that location convenience for daily deposits matters, and that feedback has been relayed to the local branch alongside other counties.

keyVotes.background: Budget and Management Analyst Jennifer Wright recommended approval of amendments 38, 40, 43, 44, 46, 47, 50, 51, 52 and 53, noting the others had already been approved. They included a $452,251 Public Health addendum for Hurricane Helene recovery, an $85,000 transfer to Facilities Maintenance, $75,000 in Disaster Energy Assistance for Social Services, and several small departmental reallocations.
keyVotes.discussion: Chairman Chappell thanked Ms. Wright for a clear presentation and for identifying the items already acted on.

topics.text: Asked the Sheriff what triggers a home visit by a school resource officer.
Asked about the role of nonprofit organizations in the jail-based reentry program.
Shared NC Association of County Commissioners concerns that vape products are unregulated and urged public awareness, especially regarding children.
Asked about the Sheriff's Office helping the understaffed Brevard Police Department.
Asked what services for exceptional students include, how much lottery money the school system has, and how the County ranks in local school funding.
Asked whether student bus usage is tracked and about the school system's electric buses.
Expressed concern about upfitting courthouse shell space while court is in session, citing past disruptions at the existing courthouse.
Encouraged the courthouse architect to produce visual materials to share with the public as soon as possible.
Asked how long the County had banked with First Citizens and whether staff had explored better rates elsewhere.
Requested that the Clerks Week proclamation be read aloud and recognized Clerk Trisha Hogan's service as President of the NC Association of County Clerks.
Said the NCACC District 16 meeting was a success and thanked staff for helping coordinate it.

Reported attending a public input session on a proposed roundabout at Cascade Lake Road and Highway 276, said social media posts about it were inaccurate, and explained it is funded through a carbon reduction program and needs no property acquisition.
Thanked Clerk to the Board Trisha Hogan for 18 years of service.
Noted that narcotics seizures had increased while Narcotics Task Force membership decreased, and thanked the Sheriff's Office.
Asked whether the five-year school security system cost included maintenance and what happens afterward.
Asked about the timeline for activity buses and whether their cost could be split over two fiscal years.
Asked whether the plan to centralize school furniture purchases was a one-time shift.
Asked whether lottery funds could be used for the school security system.
Commented that legislative changes under discussion in the General Assembly, including changes to dedicated usage amounts, could affect County water planning.
Commended the Finance Department for completing its audit under tight deadlines and during Hurricane Helene.

Said he had originally supported courthouse shell space for a third floor but changed his position based on fiscal considerations and architect input, and stressed choosing an option that allows future expansion.
Thanked staff, citizens and stakeholders for their input on the courthouse planning process.
Thanked Senator Corbin for his advocacy on broadband expansion in Western North Carolina.
Reminded the public of a National Day of Prayer gathering at the Courthouse Gazebo.
Asked about the jail housing inmates from other jurisdictions and about the jail's capacity.
Asked how the Sheriff's Office transition from Explorers to Tahoes for patrol vehicles was going.
Asked how the County's tier status affects school funding.
Asked about the planned watershed intake capacity and confirmed it would exceed 7 million gallons per day.
Said he appreciated the clear structure of the Sheriff's Office and school system budget presentations.
Asked how much fentanyl is lethal, whether fentanyl seizures had increased, and whether the border situation would affect drug flow.
Asked about the projected increase in court days for 2025.
Asked how long it takes to receive a new Sheriff's vehicle once ordered.
Asked about the failing elevator at Rosman Middle/High School, stressed the importance of accessibility, and said she would rather see urgent requests like this brought to the Board sooner.
Asked about licensing requirements for the proposed school employee childcare program.
Asked about the timing of a lottery fund request for the school security system, and whether a down payment is required for new activity buses.
Noted that the total school request was a 9% increase and asked whether the $14,987,293 figure was strictly for operations.
Expressed appreciation for collaboration between the Superintendent and the County Manager on the budget.
Commended Finance Director Meagan O'Neal for her professionalism and her presence at the Emergency Operations Center during Hurricane Helene.
Asked about the status of a regional water authority and whether part of the State allocation could support it.
Asked about the courthouse design timeline and whether 3D renderings would be provided.
Argued that phased courthouse construction is common and that a 45,000 sq. ft. building is the most cost-effective option meeting County needs, noting constituent concerns about cost.
Said the Board must begin planning for the future use of the existing courthouse.
Said it was rewarding to see Communications Director Cameron Sexton receive the Hometown Hero award at the NCACC District 16 meeting.
Responded to public comment by saying County facilities are well used and there are no surplus buildings for sale, citing the courthouse investment as evidence of space needs.
Agreed that the Sheriff's Office and school system presentations were among the best the Board has received.

publicComments.speaker: Bruce Gleasman
publicComments.summary: Suggested the County consolidate staff into fewer buildings and sell unused buildings. He estimated savings of $3 million to $6 million and urged the County to pursue the lowest tax rate in North Carolina.

publicComments.speaker: Hannah Bowers
publicComments.summary: Speaking for the Living Wage Coalition of Transylvania County, said nearly one-third of County employees earned less than a $17.55 hourly living wage in 2024, a higher share than in neighboring counties. She urged the Board to raise the County wage floor to that level, citing employee stability and retention.

publicComments.speaker: Kristi Brown
publicComments.summary: The Clerk of Superior Court asked the Board to consider where court personnel and sessions would be housed during any future courthouse expansion, noting expansion cannot occur while court is in session. She also commended the Clerk's and Magistrate's offices for 100% scores on recent audits.

publicComments.speaker: Kristi Brown
publicComments.summary: In the second public comment period, thanked the Board for voting to move forward with the courthouse project and for recognizing that a new facility is needed.

followUps.description: Release a revised project timeline for Brevard High School Scope #1 after NCDPI approval of the resubmitted plans.
followUps.resolution: Mr. Allison reported a timeline for Brevard Area Scope #1 (old gym): substantial completion by the end of October and occupancy by late November.

followUps.description: Bring the Rosman retaining wall funding request to the Board, tentatively in May.
followUps.resolution: The Rosman High School retaining wall request was brought to the Board, which allocated $652,780 from the Education Capital Fund.

followUps.description: Bring the Brevard Elementary and Rosman Elementary playground funding and contract requests to the Board, tentatively on May 12.
followUps.resolution: The Board approved the Brevard Elementary playground contract at this meeting, and the capital update reported the Rosman Elementary playground contract as approved.

followUps.description: Bring a request for additional funds for the HVAC ESSER/County-funded project balance to the Board after it goes to the Board of Education in May.
followUps.resolution: The school system's request for an additional $242,415 for HVAC projects was brought to the Board, which tabled it pending review of the school fund balance.

followUps.description: Bring a proposal for next steps on storage tank mitigation at Brevard High School.
followUps.resolution: The Board approved the $324,200 S&ME underground storage tank removal project, which includes remediation at Brevard High School where pre-removal testing showed a chemical alert in the soil.

followUps.description: Continue brief presentations over the next several meetings on key elements of the County capital plan ahead of the capital workshop.
followUps.resolution: The Manager presented the first monthly capital update, which will be given at the second regular meeting each month and posted online.

followUps.description: Provide a revised courthouse timeline once design begins, and provide visual materials such as 3D renderings with Board involvement in the aesthetic design.
followUps.resolution: Sizemore Group presented updated elevations and a design schedule. Construction documents run through April 20, 2026, permit drawings are due to the City by May 18, 2026, and construction is estimated at 18 months, with groundbreaking expected late summer or early fall 2026.

warnings: Check — followUpUpdates[2025-03-24-fu-2]: The minutes do not clearly show the requested life-cycle cost analysis of maintenance costs for traditional versus precast construction. They record only a general recommendation on construction method based on cost-effectiveness. Marking the item in_progress on this basis is a judgement call; leaving it open may be safer. (minutes: "The architectural team evaluated alternative construction methods and recommended proceeding with a traditional construction approach as the most cost-effective option at this time." (p. 22))

Check — tldr: The tldr calls the two supplement proposals "teacher supplement options", but both options apply to all school staff, not only teachers. (minutes: "Option A • 9% for all staff • 9.5% for staff with 25+ years of service" (p. 11))

Check — tldr: The tldr says the Board "approved" the third-quarter financial report. The motion was to receive the report; only the budget amendments were approved. (minutes: "Commissioner McCall moved to receive the FY 2025 3rd Quarter Financial Summary report." (p. 24))
